 Create with Anna

Try the Anna edition for AI-assisted editing and project continuity:

- Describe your edit to Anna, review a plan based on your brief and clip metadata, then apply supported clip ordering and simple 1× video trims.
- Projects and media save automatically to Anna cloud storage and can resume with the same Anna account in another browser. Local project checkpoints provide an additional recovery option.
- Refine the editable multi-track timeline, add AI voiceovers and manual captions, and export MP4 using an available browser encoder.

This desktop preview plans from metadata, without analyzing video frames or audio; local AI features depend on the Anna container’s capabilities.

→ Try Timeline Studio on Anna

遇到任何问题，欢迎扫码进群交流。我们急需你的建议和反馈！

Run into any issues? Scan the QR code to join our WeChat group. We really need your suggestions and feedback!

 

 Responsible use of deep synthesis

This tool uses deep-synthesis technology and is intended solely for technical research and learning.

Users must ensure that they:

- use only facial images or videos of themselves or people who have provided lawful authorization;
- do not create or distribute any illegal, infringing, false, or misleading content;
- do not present generated content as authentic footage or impersonate another person without their consent.

Users are solely responsible for any legal liability arising from violations of these requirements.

 Project updates

- 2026-11-13 — Video imports extract timeline thumbnails in batches. Preview updates follow playhead dragging more closely, with the same frame timing. The playhead does less work while dragging, especially in projects with many clips.
- 2026-11-10 — The Media library now has 120 sound effects to search, preview, and add to the timeline. Sound effects and music share one curve. Drag its middle to adjust volume and the two end points to set fade-in and fade-out. Memory Vortex Beats adds sound effects at key beats. Dragging a selection shows an alignment guide and snaps the group without changing clip spacing.
- 2026-11-09 — Added two editable beat templates. 3D Perspective Beats uses four opening strips and 16 independently replaceable picture-in-picture cards. Memory Vortex Beats assembles a stained-glass tunnel from the 48 slots’ photos or video stills, then plays those shots in full. Desktop Color Wheels now includes an RGB parade for checking graded SDR levels. Offline 4K export loads active media on demand and reduces memory pressure when writing large MP4 and MOV files.
- 2026-11-08 — Drag either handle in the Replace Clip dialog to adjust its source boundary, or drag the selected range to move it without changing its length or playback speed. The close icon stays centered on desktop and mobile. The properties panel follows the selected clip in the timeline and preview, and picture-in-picture settings scroll through the available panel height. Visual clip selections are outlined in the preview, and diamonds mark keyframe times on Visuals and Overlay clips. VFX lane labels fit the sidebar, and dragging the playhead uses a lighter effects preview. Added Spinning Cards, an editable square template with a four-suit neon intro, ten replaceable beat cuts and a tempo-matched soundtrack. Drag a diamond on a Visuals or Overlay clip to retime that keyframe. Spinning Cards can now display photos or video on each rotating suit. Four new editable templates add a seven-panel intro, neon film orbit, concentric ripple cuts, and staggered mask cuts. WebMCP can now preview and append beat templates, inspect timeline effects, and set mask transitions. The Timeline Studio Skill documents the workflow.
- 2026-11-07 — Added a Templates workspace after Special Effects. Use your own pictures, video and optional music in the editable three-panel montage, and set its tempo before adding it to the timeline. Halftone and multi-panel preview now play more smoothly. The template settings are in the right inspector, with a built-in soundtrack that follows the BPM. Right-click a main or picture-in-picture clip to replace it with a selected range from another source while keeping its timeline timing. Preview decodes the next shot and upcoming picture-in-picture clips ahead of their cuts for smoother playback. The replacement dialog shows thumbnail cards, a custom horizontal scrollbar for more than four assets, and the playback rate needed to fit the selected source range.
See the public Roadmap for planned work, Releases for shipped changes, and Issues for focused tasks and bugs.

 What can it produce?

Explore reproducible before/after examples and editing recipes:

→ AI Video Editing Skills Handbook

 
 
 
 

Timeline Studio is a local-first AI video editor that runs in the browser. It combines a CapCut-style multi-track timeline with WebGPU AI music and repair, multilingual voiceovers, automatic captions, talking-avatar generation, and deterministic offline export.

Open the editor · Watch on YouTube · Hugging Face Space

 Video demo

 Codex edits a three-panel beat template

Codex proposes a three-panel beat edit through WebMCP. Review and apply the plan, adjust a picture-in-picture keyframe by hand, and export the result. This 37-second demo uses Chinese narration generated locally in Timeline Studio.

 

 Auto Edit

Visual analysis, keyframes, captions, and export.

 

 AI Repair

Timed watermark removal with before/after review.

 

 AI Voiceover

 

 

 AI capabilities

- Multilingual voiceover: Chinese and mixed Chinese/English Hojo TTS Light 80M FP16 reference voices (晴岚 and 若溪), with autoregressive generation on WebGPU and stable waveform decoding on WASM; English Kokoro 82M; and browser Piper voices for German, Spanish, French, Italian, and Brazilian Portuguese.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Requirements: Node.js 20+ and a modern Chromium browser. WebGPU is recommended for the heaviest AI workflows.

git clone https://github.com/MartinDelophy/ai-video-editor.git
cd ai-video-editor
npm install
npm run dev

Open the local URL printed by Vite. The first AI run may download model files; later runs reuse the browser cache.
